### Precept Upon Precept: A Common (and Serious) Problem in Bible Study
Author: Abigail Dodds
Site: Desiring God
URL: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/precept-upon-precept
Passage: Isaiah 28:13
Points:
- The phrase "precept upon precept, line upon line" is commonly misapplied as a commendation of sound Bible study.
- In Isaiah's original context, the phrase represents babyish babble and divine judgment on prideful leaders.
- A mechanical, checklist-style approach to Scripture can cause readers to miss the larger message entirely.
- Genuine learning from God requires listening attentively so that truth bears fruit in active obedience.

### Taking Care of Mom
Author: Shirley Dobson and Dr. James Dobson
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/daily-devotions-for-parents-by-dr-james-dobson/dr-dobsons-parenting-devotional-nov-1.html
Passage: Isaiah 28:12
Points:
- Caring for small children brings demanding, exhausting, and messy days.
- Just as soil needs regular rest to stay productive, parents need intentional times of refreshing.
- Taking time for fellowship, personal interests, and quiet time with God restores emotional and spiritual energy.
- Spouses should actively support one another in carving out necessary space to rest.

### Bible Pathways 08/06/2003
Author: Bible Pathway Ministries
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/biblepathways/bible-pathways-08-or-06-or-2003-1212796.html
Passage: Isaiah 28:1-3
Points:
- The northern kingdom of Israel enjoyed material wealth and ease while turning away from God to idols.
- Isaiah cautioned that Ephraim's glorious splendor was merely a fading flower soon to be trampled.
- Complacent and worldly hearts frequently deceive themselves into thinking divine judgment will never fall.
- Believers are called to turn from sin and warn others before it is too late.
